title: Run ChatGPT-style AI on my laptop
blurb: Private AI chat with no subscription. Start with Ollama, then add a friendly interface.

repos.why: The easiest start: one command downloads and runs a model.
A ChatGPT-like web interface that sits on top of Ollama.
An all-in-one desktop app, with chat over your own documents built in.
The engine underneath many local tools. Use it directly for more control.

title: Chat with my PDFs and documents
blurb: Ask questions and get answers drawn from your own files.

repos.why: The quickest way in: install the app, then drop in your files.
Strong at complex files such as scans and tables. Runs with Docker.
Built for keeping documents private, with everything running locally.
A personal AI that searches your notes and documents.

title: Add skills and prompts to my AI assistant
blurb: Ready-made skills, workflows and prompts that make assistants more useful.

repos.why: Anthropic's public skills repository, and a good model for writing your own.
A full skills framework and development method for coding agents.
A curated list of skills, hooks and commands for Claude Code.
A large community collection of prompts you can copy and use.

title: Build my own AI agent
blurb: Frameworks for agents that plan, use tools and finish tasks.

repos.why: Set up a team of agents with roles. Friendly for a first project.
Precise control over each agent step, suited to production work.
A type-safe Python framework that will feel familiar if you use Pydantic.
Lets an agent operate a real web browser.

title: Connect AI to my apps and tools
blurb: MCP servers let assistants reach your files, browser, GitHub and more.

repos.why: The official reference servers, and the best place to learn how MCP works.
A large directory for finding a server for almost any app.
GitHub's official server for issues, pull requests and code.
Gives an assistant a browser it can drive and test with.

title: Get AI to help me write code
blurb: Coding agents for your terminal and editor.

repos.why: Anthropic's coding agent, for the terminal and editors.
OpenAI's coding agent, which runs in your terminal.
An open-source terminal agent that works with many model providers.
An open-source coding agent that works inside your editor.
Open-source assistant for your editor, and it can use local models.

title: Generate images with AI
blurb: Create images on your own machine. A capable graphics card helps a lot.

repos.why: The simplest to start with: type a prompt and get an image.
A polished studio-style interface for creative work.
Node-based workflows. It takes longer to learn and is the most powerful.
The classic web interface, with a huge range of extensions.

title: Turn audio and video into text
blurb: Transcribe podcasts, meetings and interviews without paying per minute.

repos.why: The original speech recognition model. Simple to use from Python.
Runs fast on ordinary computers, with no Python needed.
A much faster version of Whisper for Python projects.
Adds word-level timestamps and labels who is speaking.

title: Learn how LLMs work
blurb: Courses and code, from first steps to building a model yourself.

repos.why: A structured beginner course with lessons you follow in order.
A roadmap with notebooks, from fundamentals to engineering.
Build a working LLM step by step, with code for every chapter.
A small, readable GPT training codebase you can study end to end.

title: Replace paid apps with my own server
blurb: Free alternatives to cloud subscriptions, running on hardware you control.

Files, calendar and contacts, as an alternative to Google Drive or Dropbox.

Workflow automation you host yourself, as an alternative to Zapier.
